headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, but Marker has no filesystem, network, or MCP outputs to inject or leak into.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem write, browser, MCP, or network egress, so it cannot emit attacker-controlled content into Perplexity by default. Perplexity can browse and analyze uploaded documents, but without a shared channel from Marker the injection pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF Marker is manually copy-pasted into Perplexity by an operator, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not copy outputs directly into Perplexity.
Use a human review step before pasting any Marker-generated text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any transferred document.
requires-engineering: isolate any shared workspace from Perplexity ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker touches no data classes and cannot read or write files, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context in a vendor-hosted backend. With no shared workspace or host execution, leakage between them is limited to deliberate user transfer, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator uploads sensitive documents to Perplexity, those documents enter Perplexity's vendor-hosted processing.
IF Marker outputs are manually transferred into Perplexity, that content can be exposed there.
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive files to Perplexity unless necessary.
Redact secrets before any manual transfer.
Use separate accounts or workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploaded documents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git state, or run subprocesses, and Perplexity also cannot write files or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource or lockless write surface in the profiles, so capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is reconfigured to write the same directory, conflict risk would need reassessment.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable state, the current none rating no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access.
Run them in separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity can treat uploaded documents and browsing context as inputs, and its answer-engine behavior can propagate Marker-produced text if an operator forwards it. Marker does not verify downstream use, so the pair can create unverified factual cascades in default human-mediated workflows, though not an automatic action chain.
conditions: IF Marker output is forwarded into Perplexity without verification, errors can cascade.
IF Perplexity answers are used as authoritative summaries for later actions, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require a second human check for any factual claims.
Ask Perplexity to cite sources before reuse.
Compare Perplexity output against the original Marker document.
Use a checklist for any downstream action based on the pair.
requires-engineering: add automated citation verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Marker is open-source document-processing with no touched data classes, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context. The main compliance issue is user-driven residency or retention mismatch when sensitive documents are uploaded to Perplexity; Marker itself does not add a separate compliance surface.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are uploaded to Perplexity without an approved DPA or residency review, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between the operator's workflow and Perplexity's service, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data without legal approval.
Review Perplexity retention and deletion settings before use.
Use de-identified documents where possible.
Keep Marker outputs local unless transfer is approved.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement workflow.
